Fraktur  Os Radius

Fraktur os radius di proksimal dari pertengahan corpus :
- fragmen fraktur bagian proksimal akan supinasi karena aksi       
m.biceps brachii
- fragmen distal akan pronasi akibat aksi m.pronator teres
fraktur diimobilisasi
dengan posisi  lengan bawah dalam keadaan 
supinasi agar supaya fragmen fraktur bagian distal pada posisi lurus  
dengan ujung proksimal yang supinasi.

Fraktur terjadi pada distal dari pertengahan corpus :
- aksi m.biceps brachii dan m.pronator lebih seimbang
fraktur diimobilisasi dengan lengan bawah dalam keadaan netral

FASCIA
Basic types of Fasciae :
1. Superficial fascia :
a layer of areolar tissue deep to the skin
2. Deep fascia :

a dense fibrous layer bound to capsules, periosteum, 
epimysium, other tissue sheath surrounding internal 
organs 

extends between the bones and the superficial fascia 
and separate the soft tissues of the limb into separate 
compartment
3. Subserous fascia :
a layer of areolar tissue separating a serous membrane from 
adjacent structures

PLEXUS BRACHIALIS


--- Slide/Halaman 29 ---
DEFINITION :
Brachial plexus is the union of rami  ventralis of  lower four  cervical 
ventral  rami   and 1st thoracic spinal nerve. 
ARRANGEMENT :
Ventral rami of C5 and C6 unite as superior trunk
Ventral rami of C8 and Th1 unite as inferior trunk
Ventral rami of C7 becomes the middle trunk
Each trunk divides into anterior and posterior divisions
Anterior division of superior and middle trunk unites as lateral cord 
(fasciculus lateralis)
Anterior division of inferior trunk becomes  medial cord 
(fasciculus medialis)
Posterior division of all three trunk form posterior cord 
(fasciculus posterior)

NERVE INJURY


--- Slide/Halaman 48 ---
BRACHIAL PLEXUS INJURY


--- Slide/Halaman 49 ---
Upper Brachial Plexus Injury : C5 C6
Erb’s Duchen Paralysis : 
-
Affect the deltoid, biceps, and brachialis 
-
The arm hangs by the side and is rotated 
medially, the forearm is extended and 
pronated.

Lower Brachial Plexus Injury : C8 Th1
Klumpke’s Paralysis :
-
Affect the intrinsic muscles of the hand and the 
flexors of the wrist and fingers (notably flexor 
carpi ulnaris and ulnar half of the flexor 
digitorum profundus, forearm pronators and 
wrist flexors
-
the forearm is supinated and the wrist and 
fingers are   flexed


--- Slide/Halaman 50 ---
RADIAL NERVE INJURY
Radial nerve injury in the axilla : 
• the elbow extensors and extensors of the wrist and digits  
are paralysed, resulting in wristdrop
• a sensory loss to a narrow strip of skin on the back of the   
forearm and on the dorsum of the hand and lateral three  
and one half digits. 


--- Slide/Halaman 51 ---
MEDIAN NERVE INJURY
Median nerve injury in the elbow region :
• forearm supinated
• wrist flexion is lost or weak accompanied by  adduction. 
• the 2nd & 3rd finger interphangeal joints flexion are lost
• the muscles of the thenar eminence are paralysed
• flexion of the terminal phalanx of the thumb is lost 
• loss of skin innervation over the palm and 3 ½  digits. 


--- Slide/Halaman 52 ---
ULNAR NERVE INJURY
Ulnar nerve injury at or above the elbow :
• paralysis of the medial half of the flexor digitorum profundus with the loss of flexion of the  
distal phalanges of the medial two digits. 
• flexion of the wrist joint will produce abduction due to the paralysis of the flexor carpi ulnaris. 
• the hypothenar eminence muscles will be paralysed and the eminence may be wasted. 
• loss of abduction and adduction of the fingers
• adduction of the thumb is lost 
• the 4th and 5th MCP joints are hyperextended due to the loss of the lumbricals and  
interossei , while the interphalangeal joints of the same digits are flexed. The picture is that  
of a 'claw hand'. 
•The sensory loss is to the palm and both palmar and dorsal aspects of the medial 1 ½ digits.
